newsitem.title: CANADA: Inmet Copper Range suspension may hurt Q3.
newsitem.headline: Inmet Copper Range suspension may hurt Q3.

text.p: Inmet Mining Corp's decision to suspend pilot mining at its Copper Range project in Michigan may mean a third-quarter writedown, a company official told Reuters on Tuesday.

"There may be a writedown in connection with the solution mining operations and the changed circumstances at Copper Range," general counsel Peter Rozee said in a telephone interview. "It's under review."
Inmet said earlier today it was suspending its pilot scale solution mining operations in White Pine, Michigan, because of "regulatory uncertainy."
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency told the company previously that it would put approval of the pilot project on a fast track due to wrap up by July 1997, Rozee said.
But pressure from native and environmental groups prompted the agency to order a full-length environmental analysis, which is expected to last at least 18 months, he said.

"In light of that reversal, Copper Range has revisited whether it's plausible to spend the money necessary to run the pilot plant until there's more certainty as to whether the EPA is going to commit," he said.
He said Inmet had invested C$15 million in the project.
The net book value of capital assets at Copper Range at the end of last year was C$23.5 million, Rozee said. He would not say how much of a writedown the suspension would mean.
"Certainly there will be a review of the carrying value of our solution mining investment as a result of this regulatory uncertainty," he said.
Even if environmental approvals are granted in 18 months, the company will still need an additional two years to bring Copper Range into production using the solution mining method.
The company expected the project to produce 60 million pounds of copper a year, Rozee said.
Inmet suspended full-scale conventional mining at Copper Range in 1995 because it was not economic. The company expects the new solution mining process to make the operation more profitable.
The suspension of the pilot project is the company's first major move since the company's new president, Bill James, moved to Inmet from Denison Mines Ltd last month.
